data.description:

The Two Stories Investors Had To Weigh On Bilibili

The shares cost US$28.89 at the start of the period, and anyone looking at Bilibili then had to choose between two sharply different stories that both sounded plausible.

The bullish view anchored on a Fair Value of US$36.98. This price level was implied by assumptions that AI-driven ad upgrades and durable marquee games would support above-industry advertising and e-commerce growth and lift profit margins from 0.8% to 13.7% by around 2028.

The bearish camp pointed to a Fair Value of US$19.94 and focused on China’s shrinking youth population and heavier regulation. This view argued that a smaller core audience and higher compliance costs could restrain user growth and keep long term profitability under pressure even if margins rose.

What The Results Changed For The Bilibili Debate

Bilibili’s Q2 2026 results gave bulls some support. Revenue moved from ¥7,337.69m in Q2 2025 to ¥7,939.92m in Q2 2026, and net income excluding extra items rose from ¥219.00m to ¥343.73m. Net margin shifted from 3.0% to 4.3%, which helped the profitability story but left a big gap to both camps’ long term margin ambitions. Overall, the evidence cut both ways.

The real lesson is where to look next time. The whole debate hinged on margin expansion, so the key test is whether net margin and absolute profit move together over several quarters, not just whether revenue grows or the share price moves.

What The Fall In Bilibili’s Price Now Asks You To Believe

Bilibili trades at US$14.44, with the selected Narrative’s Fair Value sitting above that level based on its own assumptions rather than any proven reality. The argument leans on strong engagement, AI tools for ads, and more varied income streams alongside cost control.

The key question is whether a buyer today believes that user engagement, AI-driven monetization, and diversification can support the kind of sustained profitability the Narrative sketches out. That is what would need to be true for this past year’s 49.4% fall to look like an opening rather than a warning.
